passage: As the anthem began at the Toronto school assembly, Oskar whispered a silly rhyme about its words. Chen snorted, then held his breath, shoulders shaking. Everyone else in the row stood still. Chen glanced sideways at a girl in the next row, one hand flat on her chest, her eyes shiny. His giggle died. He stared at his shoes until the last note. At recess Oskar started the rhyme again. "Tell me later," Chen said. "Not during the song." Oskar shrugged. "It's just funny." "I know it is," Chen said. "Later."

qa.q: What did Oskar whisper during the anthem?
qa.a: Oskar whispered a silly rhyme about its words.

qa.q: What made Chen stop giggling, and how might he have felt afterwards?
qa.a: He saw a girl with a hand on her chest and shiny eyes, so he realised the anthem mattered a lot to some people; he probably felt a bit sheepish.

qa.q: What could Chen do next time a friend jokes during the anthem?
qa.a: Ask the friend to save the joke for later, as he did, and stay quiet and still himself.

qa.q: How might Oskar see Chen's request?
qa.a: As harmless fun being turned down; Oskar shrugged and said it was just funny, so Oskar may have been a little surprised or put out.

grounding: Illustrates a child giggling at the anthem because friends do, then noticing others' feelings and saving jokes for later.
